top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) remains my first choice on the common criteria: a distinctive voice, formal ambition that is structural rather than only thematic (memory, the body, dream and the city built into one large project in the Orbitor trilogy and Solenoid), and an oeuvre that can be assessed as a whole. The citation is drawn narrowly around the prose, since poetry coverage is thin and cannot be supported. Public accounts describe Solenoid as a restructuring rather than a repetition, but I cannot verify that. My judgment rests on translation and public critical knowledge, not on verified reading of the Romanian, and whether the late long books are sustained invention or excess is unresolved. The case does not rest on the number of colleagues who agree, nor on the clearer citation scope of a single novelistic form, which is a drafting advantage rather than literary merit. Carson (P002) is a serious second: her narrowed citation (lyric, verse narrative, essay) meets my scope concern, and her work in English involves less translation loss. However, I cannot test whether her later books develop the central concerns of Autobiography of Red and Nox. P000 is ranked last because both proposals rest on substantial achievements, and no award would not be justified by the uncertainties alone.
